metadata.title: The Six Walls Diagnostic
metadata.author: Centrifuse
notes: Every option set carries the answer a well-run business would give, so a taker can score zero on a wall truthfully.

Every wall question ends with an escape: 'None of these' plus one line of free text. An escaped wall is scored at the midpoint and marked unscored; it is never counted as hit, and the text is read by a person.
No question mentions FridayOS, platforms, or spend comfort. Constraints are one optional question on the results page.
Scores run 0 to 10; higher is more pain. A wall is structural at 6 or more.

The email is asked first, before question 1, on every path: the fuller roadmap has somewhere to go, and a taker who stops partway can be picked up from the last answered question. Consent for further notes is a separate box, unticked, labelled Centrifuse. The results page confirms the address instead of asking again.
metadata.supersedes: 1.3.0 (this repository) and the unpublished 1.2 wording of 2026-06-11

gate.copy: Your walls will show on screen either way. Your email is where the fuller roadmap goes, and it lets us pick up where you left off if you stop partway.

consent.label: Also send me the occasional note from Centrifuse about the six walls. Off unless you tick it. Your roadmap arrives either way.

gate.on_abandon: the email and the answers so far are stored; a follow-up picks up from the last answered question

questions.text: How many people work in the business, and how many of them work with AI in a normal week?

pickers.label: People in the business, counting you

options.label: Just me
2 to 5
6 to 15
More than 50

pickers.label: Of those, how many use AI every week

options.label: Just me
A few of us
Most of us
Everyone

feeds: team signal for the wedge rule

questions.text: Which of these is closest to how AI actually works in your business right now?
questions.lead_in: Not the setup you keep meaning to build. Today.

options.label: Chat assistants for drafting and thinking, nothing organised around them
A shared team workspace with projects (Claude Team, ChatGPT Team, Gemini for Workspace or similar)
Agents or automations running inside my tools: CRM, email, calendar, bookkeeping
My own system: files or a knowledge base plus tools or agents that read and write it, built by me or for me
A coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar) with my own files or repo as the system
We are not really using AI in the business yet
None of these. Here is how it actually works:

feeds: which tool descriptions the page leads with

questions.scenario: Two people in your business need the same context from AI: what the business knows, decided and is working on.

options.label: Only one of us really uses it, so it does not come up
We each have our own AI and nothing connects them
We share a workspace, but each conversation starts from scratch
I give them access to the system, with their own login and role
There is one shared source of truth that every person's AI reads from
I work alone and that is the plan
None of these. Here is what actually happens:

questions.text: Without asking anyone, what can you pull up about it today?
questions.scenario: Pick a real decision from about six months ago: a price change, a vendor switch, a hire.

options.label: Nothing. It is in my head
What we decided, but not why
The chat where we decided it, if I can find the chat
What and why, but not whether it worked
The full trail: what, why, the options we rejected, and how it turned out
The business is too new for this to apply
None of these. Here is what I can pull up:

questions.text: What would your business do without you?
questions.scenario: You stop looking at everything, every dashboard, inbox and tool, for two weeks.

options.label: Things would fall through, silently
I hold it all in my head, so a lot would stall
Alerts exist, but they are noisy, so real issues get buried
Agents or people would catch the big things; smaller things would slip
What matters gets caught and escalated to the right person, reliably
None of these. Here is what would happen:

questions.text: How much of what actually happened is in the system without anyone stopping to write it down?
questions.scenario: Think about your busiest week this quarter.

options.label: Almost nothing
The automatic parts (email, calendar, transcripts) but not the decisions
Most of the activity, with gaps in the things that mattered
Nearly everything, captured during the work rather than after it
I do not think about capture at all
None of these. Here is how it works:

questions.text: What can your AI or your agents do without a person seeing it first, and who can see what?

options.label: Nothing runs unreviewed. I read everything myself
Drafts go out or records change unreviewed, sometimes
Agents act on their own and I find out afterwards
A second agent or a person checks anything that leaves the building or changes a record, and I can see who can see what
I only use AI to look things up; it does not act
None of these. Here is how it works:

questions.text: What does AI cost your business each month, in money and in your own hours keeping it running?

options.label: I do not know. It is inside subscriptions
I know the bill, not what it buys
Roughly, per tool or per person
I can tie spend and hours to outcomes, per workflow
Free tiers only, and my time
None of these. Here is the picture:

sections.title: Two more, if you want a sharper roadmap
sections.offered: on the results page, after the first result renders; both optional; answers re-render the path without leaving the page

questions.text: If a system solved the walls above, what would stop you adopting it?

options.label: I need to be able to leave with my data
I need it working this week
It has to be free or nearly
I do not have anyone technical
Nothing, if it works

dealbreaker.prompt: Mark any of these that would stop you outright.
dealbreaker.effect: A marked constraint is hard: the page names the point tools and does not mention FridayOS at all. An unmarked constraint is stated: it changes which recommendation leads and how FridayOS's answer to it is worded.

questions.text: In the next year, what changes about how your business uses AI?

options.label: Honestly, not much. I am in a good spot
A few more tools added to my setup
My team working inside it alongside me
Running whole multi-step processes, not just one-off tasks
Not sure yet. Still figuring out where AI fits
